mainTopic: Finishing the story of לוט's daughters (מואב and עמון, and the reward for being first to a מצוה), then a new ברייתא on how the words ״מעם הארץ״ exclude the כהן משיח and the נשיא from the ordinary person's חטאת.
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing the story of לוט's daughters. ישראל may harass מואב but not make war on them, while עמון may not even be harassed, because the younger daughter modestly named her son בן עמי. רבי יהושע בן קרחה learns from the older daughter that one should always hurry to do a מצוה. Next, a ברייתא teaches that the words ״מעם הארץ״ exclude the כהן משיח and the king from the ordinary person's חטאת. רב זביד explains why the king needs this exclusion: half a כזית of חלב eaten as a commoner and half eaten as king do not combine. רבא and רבי זירא then ask what happens in related cases, and רבי זירא's question ends in תיקו. The גמרא then discusses the מומר: who cannot bring a חטאת, the difference between sinning out of appetite and sinning to spite, and who counts as a מין. Finally it turns to the משנה's line that the נשיא is the king, and proves this from the words ״ה׳ אלהיו״.

steps.title: מואב may be harassed, but עמון may not even be harassed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes contrasting how the תורה treats מואב and עמון, based on how each daughter named her son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only war against מואב is forbidden, but harassing them is allowed. The younger daughter named her son בן עמי ("son of my people"), so about עמון ה׳ told משה: "Do not harass them and do not contend with them." That means nothing at all is allowed, not even harassing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a point that began on the previous עמוד. It contrasts the limited protection given to מואב with the full protection given to עמון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מואב the פסוק forbids only מלחמה (war), so smaller harassment is still allowed. For עמון the פסוק adds "אל תצרם" (do not harass), so even harassment is forbidden. The difference is a reward for the younger daughter's modest choice of name, which hid where the child came from.

keyTerms.meaning: to harass or trouble someone, without full war
the younger daughter of לוט
"son of my people", a modest name that hides who the father was
do not contend with them (do not start a fight)
at all

phrases.english: It is [war] that is not allowed, but harassing them, he may harass them.
phrases.notes: This is about מואב. The פסוק there (דברים 2:9) forbids only war, not smaller harassment.

phrases.english: Whereas the younger one, who called him "Ben Ami",

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״אַל תְּצֻרֵם וְאַל תִּתְגָּר בָּם״,
phrases.english: He said to him: "Do not harass them and do not contend with them",
phrases.notes: דברים 2:19. Here "He" is ה׳ and "him" is משה.

phrases.english: at all; even harassing is not allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the אגדה about לוט's daughters from the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מואב is protected only from war. עמון is protected even from harassment, as a reward for the younger daughter's modesty.

steps.title: Always be first to do a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה learns from the older daughter that being first to a מצוה brings great reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין said in the name of רבי יהושע בן קרחה: A person should always hurry to be first for a מצוה. Because the older daughter went one night before the younger one, she earned royalty for her descendants four generations before the younger one's descendants.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is added to the same story. It teaches a lesson about hurrying to do a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The older daughter acted one night before her sister. As a reward, her line reached מלכות first. רות came from מואב and was an ancestor of דוד. נעמה the Ammonite married שלמה, four generations later. A small head start in a מצוה brought a large, long-lasting reward.

keyTerms.meaning: a person should always be first or hurry
something that is a מצוה
the older daughter
royalty, kingship

steps.whatToRemember: Hurrying to be first for a מצוה can bring reward that lasts for generations, as the older daughter's line reached מלכות four generations earlier.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Avin said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said:
A person should always be first for a matter of a מצוה,
for in reward for the one night
that the older one went before the younger one,
she merited to come before her to royalty by four generations.
phrases.notes: רות from מואב came first. נעמה the Ammonite married שלמה four generations later (רות, עובד, ישי, דוד, שלמה).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second lesson drawn from the same story of the two daughters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should always hurry to do a מצוה, as shown by the older daughter's reward.

steps.title: ״מעם הארץ״ excludes the כהן משיח and the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that the words ״מעם הארץ״ exclude the כהן משיח and the king from the ordinary person's sin-offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "From among the common people" comes to exclude the anointed כהן. "From among the common people" also comes to exclude the king.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts a brand-new topic by quoting a ברייתא about the ordinary person's חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about an ordinary person who sins (ויקרא ד:כז) says ״מעם הארץ״, "from the common people." The ברייתא reads this as a limit: the כהן גדול and the king are not "common people," so this sin-offering is not for them.

keyTerms.meaning: from among the common people
to exclude
the anointed כהן גדול
here, the king

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"From among the common people": to exclude the anointed priest.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:27

phrases.english: "From among the common people": to exclude the king,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new halachic topic after the אגדה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words ״מעם הארץ״ exclude the כהן משיח and the נשיא from the common person's חטאת.

steps.title: Why exclude them? They already have their own קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the exclusion is needed, since the כהן משיח already brings a פר and the נשיא brings a שעיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But weren't they already taken out? The anointed כהן is judged with a bull, and the king is judged with a male goat!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own teaching. Why do we need a פסוק to exclude people who already have a separate קרבן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה already gives the כהן משיח his own sin-offering, a פר, and the נשיא his own, a שעיר. So it seems obvious that they do not bring the commoner's female animal. That makes the extra exclusion look unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: but weren't they already excluded?
to be judged with, meaning to bring this as his קרבן
a bull
a male goat

phrases.english: But weren't they already excluded?
The anointed priest is judged with a bull,
the king is judged with a male goat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the exclusion taught in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for ״מעם הארץ״ to exclude the משיח and the נשיא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each already has his own separate קרבן, so the exclusion seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Without the פסוק, the כהן משיח might bring a commoner's offering for action alone
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the exclusion is needed for a case where the כהן משיח sins by action alone, without a mistaken ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed, because I might have thought: the anointed כהן brings a bull when he made a mistake in the law together with a mistaken action, but for a mistaken action alone he brings a female sheep or female goat. So the פסוק says: "From among the common people," to exclude the anointed כהן. "From among the common people," to exclude the king.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The פר covers only one kind of mistake, so the פסוק is needed to rule out the commoner's offering in the other case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן משיח brings a פר only for העלם דבר together with שגגת מעשה: he ruled wrongly and then acted on it. Without the פסוק, we might think that when he simply sins by mistake in action, he brings the commoner's כשבה or שעירה. ״מעם הארץ״ teaches that he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: for I might have thought
the law was hidden from him, meaning a mistaken ruling
an action done by mistake
a female sheep or female goat, the ordinary person's חטאת
therefore the פסוק teaches

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן משיח's פר covers only a mistaken ruling followed by action. ״מעם הארץ״ teaches that he does not bring the commoner's female animal for a mistaken action alone.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say the כהן משיח stops being a person who brings a חטאת. It only teaches that in the case of action alone, he does not bring the ordinary person's offering.

phrases.english: For one might have thought: the anointed priest, for a mistake in the law
together with a mistaken action, brings a bull,
but for a mistaken action alone
he brings a female sheep or female goat?
Therefore the verse teaches:
"From among the common people": to exclude the anointed priest.
"From among the common people": to exclude the king.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁיָּכוֹל: מָשִׁיחַ עַל הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר עִם שִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה מֵבִיא פַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the scope: the separate פר covers only one kind of mistake, so the פסוק is needed for the other case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For a mistaken action alone, the כהן משיח would bring the commoner's כשבה or שעירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״מעם הארץ״ excludes the כהן משיח from the commoner's offering even for a mistaken action alone.

steps.title: The exclusion still seems pointless for the king
steps.stepSummary: The answer from step 5 works for the כהן משיח, but not for the נשיא, who always brings a goat for an action-sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, the answer works for the anointed כהן. But a king brings his special goat exactly for an action done by mistake, so why would we need a פסוק to exclude him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 5. That answer explained the exclusion of the כהן משיח, but it does not explain why the king needs to be excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן משיח brings his פר only when he also gave a mistaken ruling, so an action-only sin leaves room for an exclusion. But the נשיא brings his שעיר for a plain mistaken action, so he never brings the commoner's offering anyway. The exclusion of the king still looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine, it works out (for this one case)
A mistaken action, a sin done by accident
The king or ruler, who brings a male goat as his sin-offering

phrases.english: Granted, for the anointed כהן it works;
but a king, for a mistaken action alone
is exactly what he brings his offering for!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 5 only covers half of the ברייתא's exclusion
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 5, which explained why ״מעם הארץ״ is needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The action-only case explains the exclusion of the משיח, but the נשיא brings a שעיר for action-only sins too, so his exclusion still has no use.

steps.title: A king who sinned before he was appointed
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד in the name of רבא says the case is a man who ate a full כזית of חלב as a commoner, became king, and only then found out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said in the name of רבא: The case is someone who ate an olive-size piece of forbidden fat while he was a regular person. Then he was made king, and only afterward found out. You might think he brings the commoner's female sheep or goat. The פסוק teaches us that he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives a case where the exclusion of the king is really needed: the sin happened before he became king, but he found out after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the sin was done as a commoner, you might think he still brings a commoner's offering. ״מעם הארץ״ teaches that because he is king when he finds out, he no longer brings that offering.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? It introduces a specific case that fits the text.
An olive's size, the smallest amount that counts as eating
Forbidden fat of an animal
A regular person, a commoner
A female sheep or female goat, the ordinary person's sin-offering
You might have thought

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said in the name of Rava:
What are we dealing with here?
For example, where he ate an olive-bulk of forbidden fat
while he was a commoner,
and he was appointed king, and afterward it became known to him.
It could enter your mind to say:
Let him bring a ewe or a female goat,
so the פסוק teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by finding a case where the king's exclusion matters
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the text to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because he sinned as a commoner, he should bring a commoner's ewe or female goat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since he is king when he finds out, ״מעם הארץ״ excludes him from the commoner's offering.

steps.title: That answer only works for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The case works only for רבי שמעון, who goes by when the sinner found out. The רבנן go by when he sinned, so the case fails for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is fine for רבי שמעון, who goes by the time the person found out. But the רבנן go by the time of the sin itself. What can you say according to them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב זביד's first answer. It says that answer only fits one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, his status when he finds out decides the offering, so a new king might need a פסוק. For the רבנן, his status at the time of the sin decides. He was a commoner then, so he obviously brings the commoner's offering, and the exclusion could not apply to this case.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for one opinion)
Finding out about the sin
The time of the sin itself
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: This works out well according to Rabbi Shimon,
who follows the time of knowledge,
but according to the Rabbis, who follow the time of the sin,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, and the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean "who follow".

phrases.english: what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָזֵל בָּתַר יְדִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case given in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רב זביד's case of a king who sinned before his appointment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the רבנן the time of the sin decides. He sinned as a commoner, so the exclusion is not needed for this case.

steps.title: Half before becoming king and half after
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד gives a new case: half a כזית eaten as a commoner and half after becoming king. The פסוק teaches that the halves do not join for a commoner's offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב זביד said in the name of רבא: The case is someone who ate half an olive-size of forbidden fat as a commoner, was made king, and then finished the olive-size. Afterward he found out. You might think the two halves join and he brings a commoner's female sheep or goat. The פסוק teaches us that he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first answer and gives a new case that works even for the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the sin is not finished until after he becomes king, so this case works even for the רבנן, who look at the time of the sin. You might think the two halves add up to a commoner's sin. ״מעם הארץ״ teaches that a king is not treated as a commoner, so the halves do not combine into a commoner's offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Half an olive's size, too little to bring an offering on its own
And he finished it, completing the full amount
Let them combine, join the two halves into one full amount

steps.whatToRemember: The final reason the king needs ״מעם הארץ״: half a כזית as a commoner plus half as king do not join to make him bring a commoner's offering.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב זְבִיד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Zevid said in the name of Rava:
What are we dealing with here?
For example, where he ate half an olive-bulk of forbidden fat
while he was a commoner,
and he was appointed king, and then he finished it,
and afterward it became known to him.
It could enter your mind to say:
Let the halves combine, and let him bring a ewe or a female goat,
so the פסוק teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב זְבִיד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the case of step 7 with one that survives the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: New case definition that fits all opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two half-amounts combine and he brings a commoner's ewe or female goat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Becoming king separates the halves, so they do not combine into a commoner's offering.

steps.title: Does a short time as king break up the two halves?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן: if a commoner ate half, became king, stepped down, and then ate the other half as a commoner again, do the halves join?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: Does being king cut off the two halves from each other? What is the case? He ate half an olive-size of forbidden fat as a commoner, was made king, then was removed, and then finished it. Maybe the earlier case did not combine only because he ate one half as a commoner and one half as king. Here both halves were eaten as a commoner, so maybe they combine. Or maybe it makes no difference. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question based on step 9. He asks whether a time of kingship in the middle separates two halves that were both eaten as a commoner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the halves don't combine when one is eaten as commoner and one as king. רבא asks whether the reason is the different status at each eating, or whether the kingship in between breaks the link. Step 11 tries to answer this, and step 12 rejects that proof.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him, a real question to a teacher
Kingship, being the נשיא
That it cuts off or separates
And he was removed from his position
Or perhaps there is no difference

steps.confusionAlert: In this case both halves were eaten as a commoner. The only question is whether the time as king in the middle cuts them apart.

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:
Kingship, does it interrupt between the halves?
What is the case?
For example, where he ate half an olive-bulk of forbidden fat
while he was a commoner,
and he was appointed, and removed, and then he finished it.
Maybe it is there that they do not combine,
phrases.notes: "There" means the case in step 9, where the second half was eaten while he was king.

phrases.english: because he ate half while he was a commoner
and half while he was king,
but here, where both this half and that half
he ate while he was a commoner, they combine;
or perhaps there is no difference?
What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן: נְשִׂיאוּת מַהוּ שֶׁתַּפְסִיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule of step 9 and asks how far it reaches
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a time of kingship between two half-amounts eaten as a commoner stops them from combining
steps.whyThisMatters: It asks what really stops the halves from joining in step 9: being a different person at each eating, or the kingship itself cutting them apart.

steps.title: Trying to answer the question from a case of a sinner who became a מומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer רבא's question using עולא's report of רבי יוחנן: once someone is pushed away from bringing an offering, he stays pushed away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Answer the question from what עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone ate חלב, set aside an offering, then became a מומר, and later came back, he stays pushed away, because he was pushed away once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of רבי יוחנן to try to answer רבא's question from step 10. The idea is that once someone is pushed out of a category, he does not come back into it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוחנן's case, the man lost his ability to bring the offering while he was a מומר, and coming back did not fix that. The same idea could apply to our king: becoming king pushed him out of the commoner's offering, so his two halves never join, even after he steps down.

keyTerms.meaning: Resolve it, answer the open question
He set aside an animal as an offering
He became a מְשׁוּמָּד, someone who has left Torah observance
Since it was pushed away, it stays pushed away

phrases.english: Resolve it from this
that עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
If someone ate forbidden fat and set aside an offering,
and then became a מומר, and then came back,
since he was pushed away, he stays pushed away.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּפְשׁוֹט לֵיהּ מֵהָא דְּאָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רבא's question from step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That the two halves do not join once the man's status has changed, even if he later steps down.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא in the name of רבי יוחנן: a sinner who became a מומר and then came back stays pushed away from his offering.

steps.title: The two cases are not alike
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails. A מומר cannot bring any offering at all, but a king can still bring an offering, just a different kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? A מומר cannot bring an offering at all. This king can bring an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבי יוחנן's case and shows why the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מומר was pushed away completely, so 'pushed away stays pushed away' makes sense for him. The king was never fully pushed away, because he still brings an offering (his own goat). So רבא's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (These cases are not alike)
Someone who is able to bring an offering
Someone who has left Torah observance

phrases.english: How can you compare?

phrases.aramaic: מְשׁוּמָּד לָאו בַּר אֵתוֹיֵי קׇרְבָּן הוּא,
phrases.english: A מומר is not someone who can bring an offering;
this one is someone who can bring an offering.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the king, who still brings an offering, just a different kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole comparison between the מומר and the king.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The מומר is cut off from all offerings. The king can still bring an offering, so he was never fully pushed away.

steps.title: A doubtful sin as a commoner, found out after becoming king
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רב ששת about a commoner who ate something that might have been חלב, became king, and then learned about the doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked רב ששת: if someone ate possible חלב while he was a commoner, then became king, and only then learned of his doubt, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. It is about a doubtful sin, which normally needs an אשם תלוי, instead of a definite sin, which needs a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא talked about definite sins. Now the sin is only a maybe, and the question is whether becoming king changes what he must bring.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question to a teacher)
Something that might or might not be forbidden fat
A commoner, a regular person
He was appointed (here, as king)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: רבי זירא asked רב ששת:
If someone ate possible forbidden fat while he was a commoner,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִתְמַנָּה וְנוֹדַע לוֹ עַל סְפֵקוֹ, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: and he was appointed king, and then learned about his doubt, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question, building on the רבנן and רבי שמעון disagreement from step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a man who becomes king before learning of a doubtful sin still bring an אשם תלוי?

steps.title: The question only works according to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: For the רבנן there is no question, because they go by the time of the sin and he was a commoner then. The question is only for רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the רבנן, who go by when he sinned, don't ask; he brings an אשם תלוי. Ask it only according to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows down רבי זירא's question. It shows which opinion the question really belongs to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן look at the time of the sin, and he was a commoner then, so he clearly brings the commoner's אשם תלוי. רבי שמעון looks at the time he found out, and by then he was king, so that is where the doubt is.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the opinion of
They go by the time of the sin
The offering brought for a doubtful sin

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two times: the רבנן look at when he sinned, and רבי שמעון looks at when he found out. Only רבי שמעון's view makes this a real question.

phrases.english: According to the רבנן, who go by the time of the sin,

phrases.aramaic: לָא תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ, דְּמַיְיתֵי אָשָׁם תָּלוּי,
phrases.english: don't ask, since he brings an אשם תלוי;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּי תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ – אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: rather, when you ask, it is according to רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from step 13 to רבי שמעון's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion the question in step 13 applies to.

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: Maybe becoming king changes things for a doubtful sin just as it does for a definite one. Or maybe it only matters when his offering would change, and for a doubtful sin it doesn't.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since his status changed for a definite sin, did it also change for a doubtful sin? Or maybe it changed for a definite sin only because his offering changes there. Here his offering doesn't change, so say he should bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out both possible ways to answer רבי זירא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: becoming king exempts him from a definite sin's offering, so it should exempt him from a doubtful one too. Side two: the exemption happens only because a king's חטאת is different (a goat). An אשם תלוי is the same for king and commoner, so nothing changed and he should still bring it.

keyTerms.meaning: It changed
A definite, certain sin
Or perhaps
His own offering

phrases.english: Since his status changed for a definite sin, it changed for a doubtful sin too?
Or perhaps, when it changed for a definite sin,
that is because his offering changed;
phrases.notes: A king brings a male goat for his חטאת, unlike a commoner.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּלָא אִשְׁתַּנִּי קׇרְבָּן דִּידֵיהּ,
phrases.english: but here, where his offering does not change,
say he should bring an אשם תלוי?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאִשְׁתַּנִּי לְוַדַּאי, אִשְׁתַּנִּי לְסָפֵק, אוֹ דִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the two sides of the question from steps 13 and 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does becoming king always exempt him, or only when his offering would be different?

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The question is left unresolved: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends רבי זירא's question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side is proven, so it stays a doubt whether the new king brings an אשם תלוי according to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question is left unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, a commoner who ate possible חלב and then became king brings an אשם תלוי. According to רבי שמעון, the question is left open (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from step 15 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי שמעון it stays unresolved whether the new king brings an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: 'From the common people' leaves out the מומר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the words 'מעם הארץ' in the פסוק leave out a מומר from bringing a sin-offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'From the common people' leaves out a מומר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins with a ברייתא. It learns from the פסוק that a מומר does not bring a commoner's חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a commoner's sin-offering says 'מעם הארץ.' The ברייתא reads these words as limiting the offering to regular members of the people, which leaves out the מומר.

keyTerms.meaning: From the common people
To leave out, to exclude

phrases.english: The רבנן taught:
'From the common people' leaves out a מומר.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:27

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with a ברייתא about the מומר, connected to the מומר mentioned in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'מעם הארץ' exclude a מומר from the commoner's sin-offering.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's source: only one who would turn back brings an offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בר יוסי, quoting רבי שמעון, learns from the words 'אשר לא תעשינה בשגגה ואשם' that only someone who would stop if he knew brings a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בר יוסי says in the name of רבי שמעון: from 'that may not be done, unwittingly, and he is guilty' we learn that a person who would turn back once he knows brings an offering for his mistake. A person who would not turn back does not bring an offering for his mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second view. It gives a different source for the same idea from Step 17: a person who does not care about the law does not bring a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view learned this from 'מעם הארץ'. רבי שמעון instead points to the sin being 'בשגגה', a true mistake. A real mistake belongs only to someone who would have stopped if he had known. Someone who would sin anyway is not really making a mistake, so he gets no offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who would turn back (stop) once he knows it is forbidden
An unintentional sin, a mistake
An offering, here the חטאת brought for a mistake

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole next discussion. There are now two sources for the same rule, and the גמרא will look for a practical difference between them.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon bar Yosei says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
"That may not be done, unwittingly, and he is guilty"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:27

phrases.english: One who would turn back upon knowing
phrases.notes: He means someone who would stop doing it if he found out it was forbidden.

phrases.english: brings an offering for his unwitting sin;
one who would not turn back upon knowing
does not bring an offering for his unwitting sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source for the same rule taught in Step 17 from 'מעם הארץ'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only someone who would stop sinning once he knows brings a חטאת for his mistake.

steps.title: What practical difference is there between the two sources?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference it makes whether the rule comes from 'מעם הארץ' or from רבי שמעון's words.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two views from Steps 17 and 18 ever lead to different results. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources agree that a משומד brings no חטאת. The גמרא assumes two different sources must make some practical difference, so it looks for a case where the views split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: Between the view that learns from 'מעם הארץ' and רבי שמעון's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two sources just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two sources lead to different results.

steps.title: רב המנונא: one who eats חלב on purpose but wants to bring an offering for blood
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a person who eats חלב on purpose and then wants to bring a חטאת for eating blood by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי המנונא said: the difference between them is a person who eats חלב on purpose and comes to bring an offering for blood. One master holds that since he eats חלב on purpose, he is also a משומד for blood. The other master holds that, at least for blood, he is someone who would turn back once he knows.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא answers the question. He gives a case where the two views split: a person who sins on purpose with one prohibition and makes a mistake with another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן ('מעם הארץ') look at the person as a whole. A משומד for חלב is a משומד for everything, so he gets no offering for blood. רבי שמעון looks at whether this person would stop for this specific sin. He would stop for blood, so he does bring an offering.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who breaks a prohibition on purpose, out of disregard for it
Forbidden fat of an animal
Blood, which is forbidden to eat
One master holds

phrases.english: Rabbi Hamnuna said:
An apostate for eating forbidden fat
who brings an offering for eating blood
is the difference between them.
One master holds:
phrases.notes: This is the view that learns from 'מעם הארץ'.

phrases.english: since he is an apostate for eating forbidden fat,
he is an apostate for blood too;
and the other master holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: for blood, at least, he is one who would turn back upon knowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי הַמְנוּנָא מְשׁוּמָּד לֶאֱכוֹל חֵלֶב וּמֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן עַל הַדָּם אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ over someone who eats חלב on purpose: the רבנן say he cannot bring a חטאת for blood, and רבי שמעון says he can.

steps.title: רבא says everyone agrees a משומד for חלב is not a משומד for blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב המנונא with רבא's rule that, according to everyone, eating חלב on purpose does not make someone a משומד for blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא said that everyone agrees a משומד for eating חלב is not a משומד for blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב המנונא's answer. It quotes רבא, who says nobody holds the view that רב המנונא gave to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא's difference depended on the רבנן saying a משומד for חלב is a משומד for blood. רבא says all opinions reject that. So there is no argument in this case, and רב המנונא's answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely! (opens a challenge)
According to everyone

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
that according to everyone,
an apostate for eating forbidden fat
is not an apostate for blood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's claim that the רבנן treat a משומד for חלב as a משומד for blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא says all opinions agree he is not a משומד for blood, so the two views cannot differ in this case.

steps.title: New difference: one who eats forbidden food out of appetite and made a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves the argument to a person who eats forbidden food only out of appetite and this time ate חלב by mistake. Is he a משומד?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they argue about a person who eats forbidden food out of appetite, and it got mixed up for him with permitted fat, and he ate it. One master holds: since he eats forbidden food on purpose out of appetite, he is a משומד. The other master holds: since he would not eat forbidden food if he found permitted food, he is not a משומד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב המנונא's case and gives a new difference between the two views. Now they argue about whether someone who sins only out of craving counts as a משומד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person eats forbidden food on purpose, but only when kosher food is not available. The רבנן look at what he does: he sins on purpose, so he is a משומד. רבי שמעון looks at whether he would stop: he prefers permitted food, so he would turn back once he knows, and he is not a משומד.

keyTerms.meaning: Out of appetite or craving, not out of rebellion
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
Permitted fat
On purpose
They argue

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse 'out of appetite' with a total mistake. This person really does sin on purpose sometimes. Only this particular eating, where the fats got switched, was a mistake.
steps.whatToRemember: The two views differ over a משומד לתאבון. Looking at his actions, he is a משומד (the רבנן). Looking at whether he would choose permitted food, he is not (רבי שמעון).

phrases.english: Rather, here it is about one who eats carcass meat out of appetite,
and it got mixed up for him with permitted fat, and he ate it
that is where they argue.
One master holds: since out of appetite
he eats on purpose, he is an apostate;

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ אַשְׁכַּח דְּהֶיתֵּרָא
phrases.english: and the other master holds: since if he found permitted food,
he would not eat forbidden food,
he is not an apostate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב המנונא's answer, which Step 21 rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They argued about a משומד for חלב bringing an offering for blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue about a משומד לתאבון who ate חלב by mistake: the רבנן say he is a משומד, and רבי שמעון says he is not.

steps.title: ברייתא: which sins make someone a משומד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says someone who ate חלב is a משומד, then asks who is a משומד and lists other sins. רבי יהודה adds wearing כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: one who ate חלב is a משומד. And who is a משומד? One who ate נבלות and טריפות, repugnant creatures and creeping creatures, or drank wine poured for idols. רבי יהודה says: even one who wears כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that defines a משומד by listing the sins that make someone one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first names חלב and then asks 'who is a משומד?' as if it had not already answered. It then gives a different list. רבי יהודה stretches the list to a sin that has nothing to do with eating, wearing כלאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals with a fatal injury, forbidden to eat
Repugnant creatures and creeping creatures
Wine poured as an offering to idols
Forbidden mixture, here a garment of wool and linen together

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who ate forbidden fat is an apostate.
And who is an apostate?
One who ate carcasses and fatally injured animals,
repugnant creatures and creeping creatures,
or drank wine poured for idols.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even one who wears a garment of forbidden mixture.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אָכַל חֵלֶב זֶהוּ מְשׁוּמָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: defining what a משומד is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating חלב, נבלות, טריפות, שקצים and רמשים, or drinking יין נסך, makes someone a משומד. רבי יהודה adds wearing כלאים.

steps.title: How can the ברייתא ask 'who is a משומד' after already answering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of the ברייתא and asks what it means, since it already said חלב makes someone a משומד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: one who ate חלב is a משומד. And who is a משומד? One who eats נבלות and so on. What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא's wording seems strange. This sets up an explanation that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave an answer (חלב) and then asked the question as if no answer had been given, then answered differently. The גמרא wants to know how these two parts fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying?

phrases.english: The master said:
One who ate forbidden fat is an apostate.
And who is an apostate? One who eats carcasses, etc.
What is he saying?
phrases.notes: He already said חלב makes someone a משומד, so why ask the question again and give a different list?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר אָכַל חֵלֶב זֶהוּ מְשׁוּמָּד וְאֵיזֶהוּ מְשׁוּמָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of the ברייתא in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the first answer (חלב) and the later list in the ברייתא fit together.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן explains what the ברייתא means
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: the ברייתא separates two people. One eats חלב for appetite and is a משומד. One eats it to spite and is a מין. Someone who eats things no one wants, like שקצים ורמשים, is assumed to be a מין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is what the ברייתא means. If someone ate חלב because he wanted it, he is a משומד. If he ate it to spite, he is a מין. And which משומד is assumed to be a מין just from what he does? One who eats נבילה and טריפה, שקצים and רמשים, or drinks יין נסך. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: also one who wears כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 24 by reading the ברייתא as talking about two different kinds of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to say the same thing twice. רבי יוחנן explains that the first line separates eating for appetite (משומד) from eating to spite (מין). The second line lists sins that show the person is a מין even without saying why he did them, since the list includes things like שקצים ורמשים that no one craves.

keyTerms.meaning: Because he wants it, out of appetite
To spite, to show defiance against the Torah
A heretic, someone who rejects the Torah
Without being told, assumed by default
Disgusting creatures and creeping animals that are forbidden to eat
Wine used in idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: משומד and מין are not the same. A משומד sins regularly, for example out of appetite. A מין rejects the Torah itself.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said: this is what it means:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל חֵלֶב לְתֵאָבוֹן – הֲרֵי זֶה מְשׁוּמָּד,
phrases.english: If he ate forbidden fat out of appetite, he is an apostate,
if he ate it to spite, he is a heretic.
And which apostate is assumed to be a heretic?
You must say: one who eats a carcass or a tereifa,
disgusting creatures and creeping animals, and one who drank libation wine.
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even one who wears diverse kinds.
phrases.notes: כלאים here means clothing made of wool and linen together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 by explaining the ברייתא's wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first line separates appetite (משומד) from spite (מין). The list names sins that make someone a מין by default.

steps.title: What is the difference between the opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who adds כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה really adds. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing כלאים is a Torah prohibition, so it seems the תנא קמא should agree it counts. The גמרא wants to know where the two opinions actually give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the disagreement quoted at the end of step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case do the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagree in practice?

steps.title: The difference is כלאים forbidden only by the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: They argue about כלאים that is forbidden only מדרבנן. The תנא קמא says only a Torah sin makes someone a משומד. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says כלאים is different, because everyone can see it, so even a rabbinic sin of כלאים makes him a משומד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is כלאים forbidden by the רבנן. One holds: breaking a Torah law makes him a משומד, but breaking a rabbinic law does not. The other holds: with כלאים, since his sin is public, even a rabbinic one makes him a משומד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions disagree about כלאים that is only forbidden by the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that Torah-level כלאים makes someone a משומד. The new point is about rabbinic כלאים. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that because a garment is seen by everyone, the sin is public, so it counts even when it is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: A mixture of wool and linen forbidden only by the רבנן
By Torah law
His sin is public, people can see it

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a Torah sin makes someone a משומד. They argue only about rabbinic כלאים, which רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה counts because the sin is public.

phrases.english: The difference between them is rabbinic diverse kinds.
One master holds: for a Torah prohibition he is an apostate,
phrases.notes: This first 'master' is the תנא קמא, the first opinion in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: for a rabbinic one he is not an apostate.
And the other master holds: diverse kinds,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

phrases.english: since his violation is publicly known,
even for a rabbinic one he is an apostate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about rabbinic כלאים. Because it is public, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה counts it.

steps.title: רב אחא and רבינא argue about spiting
steps.stepSummary: One says sinning to spite makes someone a מין. The other says spiting still makes him only a משומד, and a מין is only someone who worships עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about this. One says: out of appetite he is a משומד, to spite he is a מין. The other says: to spite he is also only a משומד. So who is a מין? Anyone who worships עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument between two אמוראים about where the line falls between a משומד and a מין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion agrees with רבי יוחנן's reading. The second opinion says even sinning to spite is not enough to make someone a מין. Only עבודה זרה does that.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree about it
Idol worship

phrases.english: Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about this,
one said: out of appetite he is an apostate,
to spite he is a heretic.
And one said: to spite, he is also an apostate,
rather, who is a heretic?
Anyone who worships idols.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an argument about the definitions that רבי יוחנן just gave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opinion 1: spite makes him a מין. Opinion 2: spite makes him only a משומד, and only עבודה זרה makes him a מין.

steps.title: Challenge from eating one flea
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says someone who eats one flea or mosquito is a משומד. No one wants to eat a flea, so it must be done to spite. This seems to prove that spiting makes him a משומד, not a מין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If he ate one flea or one mosquito, he is a משומד. But here it is to spite, and it still calls him a משומד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first opinion, which said that spiting makes someone a מין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody has an appetite for a flea, so eating one looks like spite. Yet the ברייתא calls him only a משומד, which fits the second opinion and goes against the first.

keyTerms.meaning: A flea
A mosquito

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל פַּרְעוֹשׁ אֶחָד אוֹ יַתּוּשׁ אֶחָד –
phrases.english: If he ate one flea or one mosquito,
he is an apostate.
But here it is done to spite,
and it calls him an apostate!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first opinion in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that sinning to spite makes someone a מין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating a flea must be to spite, yet the ברייתא calls him a משומד, not a מין.

steps.title: He wanted to taste something forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The flea case is not spite. He ate it because he wanted to know what something forbidden tastes like, which is a kind of appetite.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is where he said: I want to taste the taste of something forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the flea eater was not spiting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His goal was curiosity about the taste of a forbidden food. That is a form of desire, not spite, so calling him a משומד fits the first opinion too.

keyTerms.meaning: I will taste the taste of something forbidden

phrases.english: There it is where he said:
I will taste the flavor of something forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating a flea can only be to spite.
steps.terutzMaskana: He ate it out of a wish to taste something forbidden, which counts as appetite, so he is only a משומד.

steps.title: The משנה: who is the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the נשיא is the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the נשיא? This is the king, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic changes from משומד to the identity of the נשיא who brings a special קרבן. The משנה says the נשיא is the king.

keyTerms.meaning: The leader who brings a special חטאת when he sins by mistake
King

phrases.english: And who is the nasi?
This is a king, and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.

steps.title: Proof that the נשיא is a king, not a tribal leader
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks if נשיא could mean a tribal leader like נחשון בן עמינדב. It answers from the words 'ה׳ אלהיו', which also appear about the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'נשיא'. You might think it means a tribal leader like נחשון בן עמינדב. So the פסוק says: 'of all the מצוות of ה׳ his God'. And later it says: 'so that he learns to fear ה׳ his God'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that proves from the פסוקים that the נשיא is the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נשיא could mean any tribal leader. But both the פסוק about the נשיא and the פסוק about the king say 'ה׳ אלהיו'. This connects them and shows the נשיא is the king.

keyTerms.meaning: The leader of a tribe
Leader of the tribe of יהודה in the desert
So the פסוק teaches
Later, in another place in the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The נשיא who brings his own חטאת is the king. This is learned from the words 'ה׳ אלהיו' that appear in both places.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'Nasi'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:22

phrases.english: One might think it means the leader of a tribe
like Nachshon son of Amminadav?
The verse teaches:
'Of all the מצוות of the Lord his God',
and later it says:
'So that he will learn to fear the Lord his God'.
phrases.notes: דברים 17:19. This פסוק is about the king, and it also says 'ה׳ אלהיו'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the משנה's ruling in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נשיא is the king. This is learned from the words 'ה׳ אלהיו' that appear in both פסוקים.
